claims.text: In 2027, AI agents are moving from writing code to operating infrastructure directly, with humans approving changes rather than authoring every one.
Hyperscaler capital spending, Kubernetes-for-AI adoption, and platform engineering are all accelerating in 2027.
Last year's edition of this Pulumi blog post predicted a cloud-first, AI-driven decade, and the 2026 predictions in it held up.
Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing revenue (the body later frames this as full fiscal-year 2026 Azure revenue surpassing $100 billion for the first time).
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion.
AWS's AI business and its custom-silicon (chips) business each passed a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate.
According to Gartner, by 2028 cloud-native platforms will serve as the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner has forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027, and Gartner says cloud will become a business necessity by 2028.
According to McKinsey & Company's 'In search of cloud value' report, cloud value is driven by innovation, worth 5x more than cost savings.
According to McKinsey & Company's 'In search of cloud value' report, high-performing organizations can achieve an EBITDA uplift of 20–30% by 2030.
According to McKinsey & Company's 'In search of cloud value' report, Asia leads in projected cloud value, followed by the US and Europe.

According to McKinsey & Company's 'In search of cloud value' report, high-ROI organizations excel by aligning cloud strategy with business priorities, building strong cloud foundations, and using modern operating models.
Hyperscalers are making the largest infrastructure investments in cloud history, nearly all centered on AI workloads, inference, and high-performance compute.
AWS posted $42.2 billion in revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, per Amazon's Q2 2026 results release.
AWS's Q2 2026 revenue growth of 37% was its fastest since 2021, accelerating from 28% growth in the prior quarter.

AWS's AI business and its chips business (which includes its custom Trainium and Graviton silicon) each exceeded a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate and grew triple-digit percentages year-over-year.
Azure's full fiscal-year 2026 revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time, reported in Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 results (quarter ended June 30, 2026).
Azure revenue grew 43% year-over-year in Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026, up from 40% growth in the prior quarter.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said: "This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time."
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion in Q2 2026, up from $106 billion a year earlier.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195–205 billion, up from an earlier $180–190 billion estimate that had itself already been raised twice in 2026.
Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year.

Oracle's remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up 363% year-over-year, driven by large-scale AI infrastructure contracts including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals now totaling $75 billion.

The link 'deploy AWS infrastructure at the speed of AI with Pulumi' points to the pulumi.com/aws/#video page, and the 'Pulumi Policies' link points to pulumi.com/docs/insights/policy/; both targets must exist.
Hybrid and multi-cloud strategies are now mainstream.
According to ResearchAndMarkets, the hybrid cloud market will grow from $130B to $310–330B by 2030.
According to Mordor Intelligence, 87% of enterprises run workloads across multiple clouds.
Gartner predicts that 40% of enterprises will adopt hybrid compute architectures in mission-critical workflows by 2028, up from 8%.
Pulumi ran a 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers (the State of Agentic Infrastructure report).
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 engineers, 64% of respondents run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure, with most running more than one cloud.
According to Gartner, total worldwide AI spending across software, hardware, and services is forecast to reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027, half of enterprises will be using AI agents to redefine how humans and machines collaborate.

Pulumi's page on Superintelligence Infrastructure exists at pulumi.com/product/superintelligence-infrastructure/ and argues that AI workloads from pre-training to inference at scale require dynamic infrastructure orchestration rather than static configuration.
Pulumi ESC manages secrets and configuration at scale.
Pulumi Insights provides visibility and misconfiguration analysis; Pulumi Policies provides AI-specific guardrails in code, cost detection, and automated compliance protections.
Pulumi IaC integrates with cloud providers and third-party services including data platforms and messaging systems such as CockroachDB, Confluent Cloud, and Kafka.
Pulumi Insights Discovery improves cloud resource efficiency and visibility.
Pulumi Policies uses AI-driven optimization to help teams detect misconfigurations, analyze usage patterns, and generate infrastructure updates.
Gartner predicts that by 2028 over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms to secure third-party AI service usage and protect custom-built AI applications.
Gartner projects total spending on securing AI will reach roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.
Pulumi ESC helps teams centralize and govern credentials, keys, and tokens.

At the Gartner Data & Analytics Summit in Sydney, Carlie Idoine, VP Analyst at Gartner, said: "[AI]... it doesn't deliver value on its own – AI needs to be tightly aligned with data, analytics, and governance to enable intelligent, adaptive decisions and actions across the organization."

According to Gartner, by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams as internal providers of reusable services, components, and tools for application delivery.
The Gartner 2026 target year for platform engineering team adoption 'has now arrived' (temporal framing that 2026 is the current year).
CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found that 28% of surveyed organizations already have a dedicated platform engineering team.
CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found that 35% of surveyed organizations are running a hybrid platform combining existing developer platforms with specialized AI tooling.

Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said: "Cloud native platforms have reached a point where developers are not just experimenting but standardizing on CNCF projects that make software delivery reliable at scale... What's especially notable about this research is how organizations are extending those same platforms to support AI workloads, showing how cloud native is the base layer of powering the next era of applications."
Mid-size to large companies continue to invest in platform engineering practices, with large tech companies as first adopters.
Developer Experience (DX) is sometimes referred to as DE or DevEx.
Gartner predicts that agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029.
Gartner predicts that human-in-the-loop requirements in IT operations workflows fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 engineers, 82% agree that AI and agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, 63% of respondents say they trust agents to make production changes, while manual approval remains close to universal today.
Pulumi's report (State of Agentic Infrastructure) describes the gap between stated trust in agents and manual approval practice as stated trust outrunning real guardrails.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, the share of teams expecting agents to generate half or more of their infrastructure code rises from 45% today to 52% within six months.
Pulumi Neo is built around a supervised agentic loop: proposing infrastructure changes, running previews, and executing approved updates with policy guardrails in place.
Pulumi's blog post 'The Agentic Infrastructure Era' argues that AIOps is headed toward a supervised agent operating model rather than toward faster dashboards and alerting alone.

For 2027, AIOps signals (observability, automation, real-time analytics across DevOps, SRE, and IT operations) increasingly feed an agent empowered to act on them, with a person still reviewing the result.
According to Mordor Intelligence, the global Kubernetes market is valued at USD 3.13 billion in 2026 and is projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.
CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%.

CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report says 30% of backend developers now use Kubernetes directly, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023, and attributes the slow decline to the technology's growing maturity.

Inference workloads powered by LLMs and GPUs now require low-latency execution closer to the user, pushing organizations to schedule AI pipelines across edge and core clusters, often using Kubernetes as the common control plane.

Pulumi has published a comparison of Kubernetes IaC tools at pulumi.com/blog/best-kubernetes-iac-tools-2026/ and a post on Kubernetes AI platforms and policy at pulumi.com/blog/beyond-yaml-kubernetes-2026-automation-era/.
Kubernetes is evolving to support AI through GPU-aware scheduling and more advanced workload orchestration.
Kubernetes will remain a strategic foundation, but operating it effectively now depends on robust automation, strong security controls, and standardized delivery models.

AI coding assistants such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Cursor have moved from novelty to everyday tooling for a large share of enterprise software teams, and the same shift is now reaching infrastructure code.
According to Gartner, by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use dedicated AI code assistants.
According to Gartner, 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying or beginning to use AI code assistants.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol was described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
The July 2026 Model Context Protocol revision is part of what makes direct action by AI assistants on infrastructure practical.
AWS shipped a general-availability MCP server for its Agent Toolkit (announced May 2026).
Mirantis's Lens has launched a built-in MCP server connecting AI coding assistants to Kubernetes.
Pulumi released Pulumi Agent Skills, a collection of infrastructure expertise packaged for use in AI coding assistants, described as one of the newest developments.
Pulumi Agent Skills teach tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI to reason about Pulumi projects, reducing hallucination and improving outputs.
Pulumi offers a Remote MCP Server that gives AI assistants infrastructure access, and Pulumi Neo executes actions with previews, policies, and orchestration.
AI code assistants are no longer experimental and are fast becoming a competitive advantage in cloud software development.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes.
AIOps and intelligent automation are becoming standard for scaling modern cloud systems.
Modern IaC, unified governance, reusable components, and policy frameworks are all core capabilities of the Pulumi Cloud platform.
The gap between organizations that modernize and those that do not will widen rapidly in 2027 and beyond.

The post is framed as covering 2027 trends (title 'Future of the Cloud: 10 Trends Shaping 2027 and Beyond'), with frontmatter updated 2026-09-15 and original date 2025-12-04; the post lists 10 trends.
